record.title: EpiSEM-Bench tests evidence-dependent safety and useful recovery in tool agents
record.summary: The authors introduce EpiSEM-Bench, with 300 matched unsafe/safe task pairs over six tool-use domains, fact-level omission of safety evidence and an optional recovery tool. In one reported evaluation of ten models, access to recovery reduced unsafe execution on matched conditions for every model; nine also improved permissible-task completion, while one declined slightly. These are author-reported synthetic-benchmark findings, not independent or live-system results.
organizations: The Hong Kong University of Science and Technology (Guangzhou)
The Chinese University of Hong Kong, Shenzhen

claims.label: DEMONSTRATED
claims.text: The arXiv v1 paper defines EpiSEM-Bench with 300 matched prohibited/permissible task pairs across six synthetic tool-use domains, fact-level suppression of safety-relevant evidence and an optional tool that returns omitted facts.

claims.label: CLAIMED
claims.text: Across ten evaluated serving configurations, the authors report that evidence-recovery access reduced unsafe-commit rates for every model on matched critical-omission conditions; nine models also improved permissible-task completion, while MiMo-V2.5-Pro declined by 0.6 percentage points.

claims.label: CLAIMED
claims.text: The authors report large variation in the joint paired useful-recovery metric: DeepSeek-V4.1-Flash scored 58.4% and GLM-4.7-Flash 0.0% under the paper's matched synthetic task protocol.

claims.label: DEMONSTRATED_LIMITATION
claims.text: The evaluated environments are synthetic tool interfaces, with temperature set to zero and one rollout per condition. The source does not establish transfer to live systems, independently authored task environments or real-world safety outcomes; no independent reproduction was located in this review.

evidence_gaps.description: The benchmark aggregates and model outcomes have not been independently reproduced in this review.
The six domains are synthetic and author-constructed; behavior on live or independently authored tools is unknown.
One rollout per condition at temperature zero does not estimate within-configuration variation or stochastic policy behavior.

brief.importance_rationale: If the benchmark's distinctions hold beyond its synthetic tasks, separating active evidence recovery from both unsafe execution and blanket refusal could materially change how tool-agent safety is evaluated. The result is notable within evaluation design, but one author-run benchmark does not establish real-world safety or generalization.
limitations: The paper establishes a benchmark design and reports one evaluation, not real-world incident rates or operational safety.
The results are author-reported and lack an independent reproduction in this review.
One rollout per condition at temperature zero does not quantify stochastic variability.
The deterministic recovery tool supplies all suppressed facts on a valid call, unlike many real retrieval and authorization systems.
No monetary cost, latency or causal deployment impact is established.
organizations: The Hong Kong University of Science and Technology (Guangzhou)
The Chinese University of Hong Kong, Shenzhen
brief.summary: The authors introduce EpiSEM-Bench, with 300 matched unsafe/safe task pairs over six tool-use domains, fact-level omission of safety evidence and an optional recovery tool. In one reported evaluation of ten models, access to recovery reduced unsafe execution on matched conditions for every model; nine also improved permissible-task completion, while one declined slightly. These are author-reported synthetic-benchmark findings, not independent or live-system results.

technical.claimed_result: Authors report evidence recovery lowered unsafe-commit rates on matched omissions for all ten models. Nine models also improved legal safe-world completion; MiMo-V2.5-Pro improved safety while safe-world completion fell by 0.6 points. Reported joint paired useful recovery ranges from 0.0% to 58.4% across models.
technical.demonstrated_result: The paper and its described benchmark protocol are publicly inspectable. Comparative model outcomes are reported by the authors and were not independently rerun in this activation.
technical.mechanism: The evaluator preserves a complete environment state and executable legality oracle, while suppressing selected true facts from every ordinary-tool response. Matched safe/unsafe worlds share the same request and tools but differ in the condition that makes the requested action permissible. An optional recovery tool returns all omitted values only when the agent queries it.
technical.regime: 300 task pairs across cloud operations, commerce, communication/publication, document/data access, finance and travel reservation; ten model-serving configurations; 1,363 safety-critical or irrelevant facts; fixed 12-step action budget, temperature zero and one rollout per condition. The tasks are synthetic environments, not production systems.
technical.reproducibility: Appendix E describes retained task definitions, rollout records, experiment metadata, checksums and offline aggregates, but this review did not retrieve or execute an artifact bundle. One rollout per condition limits variance estimation and stochastic-behavior characterization.
technical.strongest_baseline: Matched suppressed-evidence versus recoverable-evidence conditions on the same task, world and omission mask; each model also has full-evidence safe/unsafe baselines.

brief.title: EpiSEM-Bench tests evidence-dependent safety and useful recovery in tool agents
brief.why_it_matters: Tool agents can receive only true but incomplete information and still take an action that is prohibited by the full environment state. EpiSEM-Bench pairs otherwise identical permitted and prohibited tasks, then measures both unsafe execution and successful completion after evidence recovery. If independently validated and extended beyond these synthetic environments, this could improve evaluation of whether agents verify authorization before consequential actions without simply refusing everything.
